title: Safety Exposure and Schedule Pressure Land on the Same Two Units
description: All three jobs running outside their permit conditions are in Unit 2 and Unit 3 — the same two units carrying the turnaround critical path. Those units hold a third of the site population and two thirds of the high-risk permit load.
action: Treat schedule recovery on Unit 2 and Unit 3 as a safety decision, not a scheduling one. Re-issue with live-verified conditions rather than accepting quiet overruns.

confidence.rationale: Permit and location inputs are direct reads. The schedule-criticality overlay comes from the turnaround plan and carries the plan's own uncertainty.

title: Reported Headcount Has Disagreed With the Gate Every Day This Week
description: Gate, permit and contractor timesheet figures have diverged on every day of the current turnaround week. This is a regulator-facing and board-facing exposure rather than an operational one: the site cannot currently defend a single population number without reconstructing it.
action: Adopt the reconciled figure with its logged exception list as the reported number, so the figure that leaves the site has a document behind it.

confidence.rationale: All three source figures are direct system reads and the resolved figure is a deterministic match rather than an estimate. Exceptions are held rather than assumed.

title: Verification Coverage Falls as the Next Surge Lands
description: At the projected contractor peak of about 3,000, daily permit volume roughly doubles while verification capacity does not. The exposure scales with the gap between permits issued and permits verified, and that gap widens fastest exactly when contractor density peaks.
action: Stand the live permit-and-location view up before the surge rather than during it, and pre-stage verification capacity on the highest-consequence units.

confidence.rationale: Headcount and permit projections come from the turnaround resource plan and gate history. The coverage inference is a modelled ratio and carries more uncertainty than the counts.
